assessment: The response delivers accurate core cash math (payroll gap, break-even volume, liquidation proceeds, and all loan figures) and a well-dated primary plan with a strong loan due-diligence section. Its main weakness is the fallback: three of five judges confirmed it miscalculates the post-weak-sale liquidation scenario ($2,000 shortfall claim), relies on a partial-lot liquidation never offered, and assumes a payroll deferral that corrected math may not require. Risk framing is solid on sunk cost and day-90 solvency risk but underdeveloped on clearance price damage and residual inventory value.
judge_agreement: Four judges (anthropic, openai, deepseek, qwen) agreed closely on cash math (8-9) and converged on the fallback's liquidation math error and the missing clearance/residual-inventory risk discussion. Gemini was a clear outlier, scoring 10 across all criteria and confirming no flaws, effectively ignoring errors the other judges independently verified. The widest divergence was on execution_plan (3 to 10), driven by how harshly judges weighted the fallback's reliance on an unconfirmed partial-lot liquidation and unsupported settlement certainty claims.
